title: fm-project.sh: managed clones, target verification and the guard
acceptance: Implements design.md sections 15.1 (managed clone) and 15.6 (what a target needs). New bin/fm-project.sh with `sync <name>` and `verify <name>`, following section 5.3.1's option rules. For the self project both are no-ops that succeed.

sync clones the project's github repository into state/projects/<name>/repo, or fetches and prunes an existing clone; sets core.hooksPath in the clone's local git config to the engine's .githooks/; adds `.fm-*` to the clone's .git/info/exclude. It writes nothing into the target's tree and never touches any checkout outside state/projects/.

verify refuses with exit 70, naming each missing item, unless: base is protected with enforce_admins on, up to date required and required_check a required status check; the repository is public (section 15.8 — private projects wait for a captain decision); the clone's hooks path is the engine's .githooks/. The gh stub answers these API calls in the shapes GitHub returns.
fm-guard.sh and the hooks protect main, master and the project's base; the self project's protected set is unchanged.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
